newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit firms in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit firms in cautious trade.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit firms as offshore players cover short positions amid rise in interbank rates after central bank warning against speculation.
* Philippine peso relatively calm after central bank raises key overnight borrowing rate to 32 percent.
* Indonesian rupiah rises, swaps fall as anxiety about instability in neighbouring markets fades.
* Thai baht driven largely by commercial demand in domestic markets, offshore players square positions.
* Taiwan dollar opens up in line with weakness in dollar/majors and tight domestic liquidity.
* Singapore dollar tracks now familiar 1.4350-1.4380 range.
The ringgit rose on Thursday as offshore players sold the dollar amid continued indications Malaysian authorities were determined to defend their currency.
A Malaysian bank dealer said there was talk Bank Negara had placed orders with agent banks to sell dollar/ringgit at 2.5050.
The central bank was said to have intervened strongly in the market on Tuesday, spending an estimated $1.0 billion to lift the ringgit.
Dealers said the dollar was quick to recover each time it dipped below 2.50, suggesting that shorts were willing to take quick profits.
They said the market was concerned that Bank Negara would re-impose capital controls to broaden its intervention tools.

The central bank on Wednesday warned of tough measures, including increasing interest rates, to stamp out speculation in the ringgit, which has come under pressure from overseas in the wake of the baht crisis.
Malaysian Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday the country's strong economic fundamentals and stability did not warrant undermining of the ringgit.

"The Malaysians are in a better position in that they have stronger forex reserves and their problems are less chronic than Thailand. My only concern is their current account problems -- they seem to keep overspending," a Singapore-based dealer said.

The ringgit was quoted at 2.4980/90 to the dollar at 0412 GMT against 2.5033/43 at its close in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. Elsewhere, the Philippine peso was relatively calm as the central bank raised its key overnight borrowing rate by two
percentage points to 32 percent, its highest in 2-1/2 years.
The peso was at 26.400/26.404 against 26.40 at its previous close as banks were still buying dollars after recent devaluation fears, dealers said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah firmed and swap premiums fell on offshore selling as fears of a Thai-style crisis spreading to the Philippines or Malaysia subsided.

Economists said relatively strong economic fundamentals seemed to have helped protect the rupiah from speculators looking for victims after recent attacks on the Thai baht, the Philippines peso and the Malaysian ringgit.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,431.5/32.5 at 0415 GMT against an opening of 2,432.3/32.8.
Some dealers said there was still speculation of a widening of the central bank intervention band, which seemed to sustain upward pressure on the rupiah.

The Thai baht was driven mainly by commercial demand in domestic markets where Thai corporates needed to service dollar debt. Offshore activity was confined to some position-squaring in the absence of fresh leads.
The baht was trading at 29.10/29.15 per dollar onshore by 0415 GMT against 29.01/29.06 late on Wednesday. The central bank's reference rate was 29.075 against 29.096 on Wednesday.
The Taiwan dollar opened sharply up on tight liquidity and weakness in the dollar/majors, dealers said.
The unit was quoted at T$27.883/888 at 0415 GMT after closing at an eight-year low of T$27.926 on Wednesday.
Dealers said investors had turned cautious as the currency approached the T$27.94 level, which used to be staunchly defended by the central bank.

-- Lilian Karunungan in Manila (632-841-8937), Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642, James Peng in Taipei (8862-508-0815) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
